market_context.summary: One story drives everything on the page, and it is a rates-and-oil story rather than an equity one. US-Iran fighting has cut Hormuz crude flows to under 2 mbpd from 8-9 mbpd pre-conflict, crude is reported near $105, and the resulting inflation impulse has the market pricing Fed HIKES rather than cuts: roughly 64% odds of 25bp in October and 48% in December against an effective funds rate still at 3.88%. The 10-year is 5.11%, a 15bp one-day backup and the highest since July 2007; the 2-year is 4.85%, so the whole curve sold off and this is not a term-premium-only move; 10y-2y has bear-steepened to +0.31. August CPI ran +0.40% m/m and the trigger was S&P Global's flash PMI showing the fastest private-sector activity in five years with stronger price pressures. Equities are not obviously breaking - a secondhand report has the Dow -0.3% on 2026-09-24, MU closed +0.8% near its highs, and energy is leading - which is why the regime is called mixed rather than risk-off. IMPORTANT: no index, VIX, DXY, gold or crude quote could be fetched this morning (Yahoo returned HTTP 429 on every index symbol, finnhub refuses indices without a CFD subscription, stooq 404s on '^' symbols), so there is no fetched index level anywhere in this report and the equity read above rests on single names plus one news citation.

recommendations.thesis: The 10-year at 5.11% is the highest since July 2007 and the 30-year at ~5.5% the highest since 2004, and the repricing is not a term-premium story but a policy story: futures now put ~64% on a 25bp October hike and ~48% on December, against an effective funds rate still at 3.88%. TLT closed at 79.42, a 250-day low, with the 20-, 50- and 200-day averages stacked above it at 81.56, 82.35 and 85.71 - every marginal holder of duration bought higher.
recommendations.key_risk: A Hormuz ceasefire or any credible de-escalation with Iran takes crude back under $90 and the whole inflation impulse with it; long-duration bonds would retrace the move faster than a stop can be honoured, and this is a gap-risk short rather than a grind. Note also that this is TLT's third appearance in ten days: the repricing is the justification, and if the red team disagrees this is the idea to cut rather than the newer ones. RED TEAM: conviction lowered 4 -> 3 and the named risk sharpened. This idea's evidence is the best-verified in the report - FRED confirms DGS10 5.11% and DGS2 4.85% on 2026-09-23, both up from 4.96% and 4.71%, so the front-end repricing the counter_argument leans on is real and fetched. But the stated de-escalation risk is no longer hypothetical: FRED DCOILWTICO has WTI at 96.41 on 2026-09-22, down from 107.02 on 2026-09-15 and through $100 on 09-21, a 10% unwind in five sessions with no ceasefire announced. The oil-inflation impulse behind the hike repricing is already fading while the trade is being re-published on it. What is left is a policy bet at exactly 2.000:1 against a 2.0 floor, on its third publication in ten days. The 2.66 ATR stop and the fact that 82.00 was set first are why this is a downgrade and not a cut.
recommendations.counter_argument: Short-duration positioning is already crowded and 5.11% is a level that has historically attracted real money - pensions and insurers buy the long end for liability matching at 5%+, which is precisely why the 2023 push through 5% failed within weeks. The answer is that 2023 had a Fed cutting into a disinflation; this one has a Fed being pushed back toward hiking, so the carry argument for catching the falling bond is materially worse.
